1:1.sourceText: Ἰούδας Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δοῦλος, ἀδελφὸς δὲ Ἰακώβου, τοῖς ἐν Θεῷ Πατρὶ ἠγαπημένοις καὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ τετηρημένοις κλητοῖς.
1:1.targetText: Judas, a servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to those called, having been loved in God [the] Father, and having been kept in Jesus Christ,

groups.note: The actual Jesus Christ dative is the complement of being kept. LSV construes it as in Jesus Christ; Greek has this dative phrase without a separately written ἐν, and its for/by/in relation is a matter of construing the keeping complement.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the definite article before Father; the actual Greek God Father phrase is anarthrous.

1:2.sourceText: ἔλεος ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη καὶ ἀγάπη πληθυνθείη.
1:2.targetText: mercy and peace and love be multiplied to you!

1:3.sourceText: Ἀγαπητοί, πᾶσαν σπουδὴν ποιούμενος γράφειν ὑμῖν περὶ τῆς κοινῆς ἡμῶν σωτηρίας, ἀνάγκην ἔσχον γράψαι ὑμῖν παρακαλῶν ἐπαγωνίζεσθαι τῇ ἅπαξ παραδοθείσῃ τοῖς ἁγίοις πίστει.
1:3.targetText: Beloved, using all diligence to write to you concerning our common salvation, I had necessity to write to you, exhorting [you] to fight for the faith once delivered to the holy ones,

groups.note: The actual writing recipients you are also the immediately stated exhortation recipients. English resumes those same people as bracketed [you] after exhorting; no independent second Greek recipient pronoun is written.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:4.sourceText: παρεισεδύησαν γάρ τινες ἄνθρωποι, οἱ πάλαι προγεγραμμένοι εἰς τοῦτο τὸ κρίμα, ἀσεβεῖς, τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν χάριτα μετατιθέντες εἰς ἀσέλγειαν καὶ τὸν μόνον Δεσπότην καὶ Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἀρνούμενοι.
1:4.targetText: for there came in certain men stealthily, having been written beforehand to this judgment long ago, impious, perverting the grace of our God to licentiousness, and denying our only Master and Lord—Jesus Christ.

groups.note: Actual genitive article and God name jointly supply of ... God as the grace qualifier. Our remains separately anchored to its actual possessive occurrence; the later Master/Lord clause is not merged into this group.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:5.sourceText: Ὑπομνῆσαι δὲ ὑμᾶς βούλομαι, εἰδότας ἅπαξ πάντα, ὅτι Κύριος λαὸν ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου σώσας τὸ δεύτερον τοὺς μὴ πιστεύσαντας ἀπώλεσεν,
1:5.targetText: Now I intend to remind you, you once having known all this, that Jesus, having saved a people out of the land of Egypt, He secondly destroyed those not having believed;

groups.note: The actual accusative you is the reminder recipient and the personal reference of the agreeing having-known participle. English names the same people twice as remind you, you ... having known.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual N1904 title Κύριος is Lord, while the pinned LSV edition explicitly names Jesus. The different written title/name readings are not treated as one lexical identity.
Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned LSV edition reads the personal name Jesus where N1904 writes the title Lord, Κύριος. The common action is mapped without replacing the actual source title.

1:6.sourceText: ἀγγέλους τε τοὺς μὴ τηρήσαντας τὴν ἑαυτῶν ἀρχὴν ἀλλὰ ἀπολιπόντας τὸ ἴδιον οἰκητήριον εἰς κρίσιν μεγάλης ἡμέρας δεσμοῖς ἀϊδίοις ὑπὸ ζόφον τετήρηκεν·
1:6.targetText: messengers also, those who did not keep their own principality, but left their proper dwelling, He has kept in eternal bonds under darkness until [the] judgment of [the] great day,

groups.note: The actual goal preposition εἰς introduces the judgment at which the keeping ends; English expresses this temporal endpoint as until, without a separately written Greek ἕως.
The actual dative bonds phrase gives the keeping circumstance, expressed as in ... bonds without a separately written Greek ἐν.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:7.sourceText: ὡς Σόδομα καὶ Γόμορρα καὶ αἱ περὶ αὐτὰς πόλεις, τὸν ὅμοιον τρόπον τούτοις ἐκπορνεύσασαι καὶ ἀπελθοῦσαι ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἑτέρας, πρόκεινται δεῖγμα πυρὸς αἰωνίου δίκην ὑπέχουσαι.
1:7.targetText: as Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities around them, in like manner to these [messengers], having given themselves to whoredom, and having gone after other flesh, have been set before [as] an example, undergoing the justice of continuous fire.

groups.note: The actual accusative manner construction is adverbial, expressed as in ... manner around the separately anchored like adjective, without a written ἐν.
The actual example noun functions predicatively with being set before; English expresses that predicative role as as an example, without a separately written ὡς.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV makes an antecedent interpretation of these explicit as messengers. The actual demonstrative τούτοις does not repeat an angel/messenger noun; the identity interpretation remains explicit rather than inventing another Greek noun.

1:8.sourceText: Ὁμοίως μέντοι καὶ οὗτοι ἐνυπνιαζόμενοι σάρκα μὲν μιαίνουσιν, κυριότητα δὲ ἀθετοῦσιν, δόξας δὲ βλασφημοῦσιν.
1:8.targetText: In like manner, nevertheless, those dreaming indeed defile the flesh, and they disregard lordship, and they speak evil of glorious [ones],

groups.note: The actual plural glories noun δόξας is construed personally as glorious ones in LSV. The English adjective/person support belongs to this nominal construction, not a separately written Greek glorious adjective or ones noun.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 includes an additive καί, also/even, before these dreamers; English does not separately print that additive word.

1:9.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Μιχαὴλ ὁ ἀρχάγγελος, ὅτε τῷ διαβόλῳ διακρινόμενος διελέγετο περὶ τοῦ Μωϋσέως σώματος, οὐκ ἐτόλμησεν κρίσιν ἐπενεγκεῖν βλασφημίας, ἀλλὰ εἶπεν Ἐπιτιμήσαι σοι Κύριος.
1:9.targetText: yet Michael, the chief messenger, when disputing with the Devil, reasoning about the body of Moses, did not dare to bring against [him] a judgment of slander, but said, “The LORD rebuke you!”

groups.note: The actual Devil is the person with whom Michael disputes and against whom the immediately stated judgment would be brought. English resumes this same disputed-with person as bracketed [him], without a separate Greek object pronoun.

Greek διελέγετο is the finite past deliberating/discussing predicate; English presents it as reasoning within the same when-disputing circumstance. The actual discourse action is retained with this finite-to-participial wording explicit.
The actual aorist optative expresses the wished-for rebuke, rendered by English The LORD rebuke you; it is not an indicative report that a rebuke already occurred.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:10.sourceText: οὗτοι δὲ ὅσα μὲν οὐκ οἴδασιν βλασφημοῦσιν, ὅσα δὲ φυσικῶς ὡς τὰ ἄλογα ζῷα ἐπίστανται, ἐν τούτοις φθείρονται.
1:10.targetText: But these, indeed, whatever [things] they have not known, they speak evil of; and whatever [they know], like the irrational beasts, they understand naturally—in these they are corrupted;

groups.note: The single actual knowledge predicate ἐπίστανται governs whatever is naturally understood. English states that same predicate twice, once as the bracketed relative-clause completion they know and once as the resumed they understand naturally; these are not two different written Greek knowing verbs.

1:11.sourceText: οὐαὶ αὐτοῖς, ὅτι τῇ ὁδῷ τοῦ Κάϊν ἐπορεύθησαν, καὶ τῇ πλάνῃ τοῦ Βαλαὰμ μισθοῦ ἐξεχύθησαν, καὶ τῇ ἀντιλογίᾳ τοῦ Κόρε ἀπώλοντο.
1:11.targetText: woe to them! Because they went on in the way of Cain, and they rushed to the deceit of Balaam for reward, and in the controversy of Korah they perished.

groups.note: Actual genitive article and indeclinable Cain name jointly supply of Cain as the way qualifier. The name retains its recorded N-PRI tag, with the genitive relation carried by the article construction.
Actual genitive article and indeclinable Balaam name jointly supply of Balaam as the deceit qualifier. Its recorded N-PRI analysis remains; the separate reward nominal relation is not absorbed.

The actual pouring-out verb ἐξεχύθησαν is used of their unrestrained movement into Balaam’s error; English renders this metaphor as they rushed, not as a claim that the original contains a distinct rushing verb.
Actual genitive article and indeclinable Korah name jointly supply of Korah as the controversy qualifier. The name retains N-PRI and remains distinct from the preceding Cain/Balaam occurrences.

1:12.sourceText: Οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἐν ταῖς ἀγάπαις ὑμῶν σπιλάδες συνευωχούμενοι ἀφόβως, ἑαυτοὺς ποιμαίνοντες, νεφέλαι ἄνυδροι ὑπὸ ἀνέμων παραφερόμεναι, δένδρα φθινοπωρινὰ ἄκαρπα δὶς ἀποθανόντα ἐκριζωθέντα,
1:12.targetText: These are stains at your love-feasts, feasting together with you without fear, shepherding themselves; waterless clouds, being carried away by winds; autumnal trees without fruit, having died twice, having been uprooted;

groups.note: The actual your identifies the community whose love-feasts these people attend; the compound feasting-together predicate states their joint participation at those same community meals. English with you resumes that actual community as the co-feasting partners. This contextual shared-community relation does not claim a separate written Greek ὑμῖν or the attendance of every individual reader.

LSV follows the spot/stain interpretation of σπιλάδες. The word is also read as dangerous rocks/reefs; the actual head and this lexical interpretation are retained rather than substituting the different Greek word σπίλοι.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:13.sourceText: κύματα ἄγρια θαλάσσης ἐπαφρίζοντα τὰς ἑαυτῶν αἰσχύνας, ἀστέρες πλανῆται, οἷς ὁ ζόφος τοῦ σκότους εἰς αἰῶνα τετήρηται.
1:13.targetText: wild waves of a sea, foaming up their own shameful [deeds]; stars going astray, for whom the gloom of the darkness throughout the age has been kept.

groups.note: The actual plural shame noun αἰσχύνας denotes their shames/shameful deeds in this image. English expresses that one nominal designation as an adjective plus bracketed deeds; no extra written Greek deed noun is claimed.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:14.sourceText: Ἐπροφήτευσεν δὲ καὶ τούτοις ἕβδομος ἀπὸ Ἀδὰμ Ἑνὼχ λέγων Ἰδοὺ ἦλθεν Κύριος ἐν ἁγίαις μυριάσιν αὐτοῦ,
1:14.targetText: And Enoch, the seventh from Adam, also prophesied to these, saying, “Behold, the LORD has come with myriads of His holy ones,

groups.note: The actual aorist came is expressed by English has come; the same coming event retains its actual head with the tense/aspect wording difference explicit.

The actual holy adjective agrees with the myriads in Greek, the holy myriads of His. English recasts this company as myriads of His holy ones; ones is nominal support for the holy members, not an independently written Greek person noun, and the attachment/case difference is explicit.

1:15.sourceText: ποιῆσαι κρίσιν κατὰ πάντων καὶ ἐλέγξαι πάντας τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς περὶ πάντων τῶν ἔργων ἀσεβείας αὐτῶν ὧν ἠσέβησαν καὶ περὶ πάντων τῶν σκληρῶν ὧν ἐλάλησαν κατ’ αὐτοῦ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀσεβεῖς.
1:15.targetText: to do judgment against all, and to convict all their impious ones, concerning all their works of impiety that they did impiously, and concerning all the harsh [words] that impious sinners spoke against Him.”

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV supplies a possessor with the first impious ones; pinned N1904 has all the impious without an independently written possessive there. The actual later αὐτῶν belongs to their works.

1:16.sourceText: Οὗτοί εἰσιν γογγυσταί, μεμψίμοιροι, κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πορευόμενοι, καὶ τὸ στόμα αὐτῶν λαλεῖ ὑπέρογκα, θαυμάζοντες πρόσωπα ὠφελείας χάριν.
1:16.targetText: These are discontented grumblers, walking according to their own lusts; and their mouth speaks swollen words, giving admiration to persons for the sake of profit;

groups.note: The actual neuter plural swollen/extravagant adjective is used substantivally of the speech. English supplies words as its nominal support; the real adjective keeps that complete designation, not a newly invented Greek word noun.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:17.sourceText: Ὑμεῖς δέ, ἀγαπητοί, μνήσθητε τῶν ῥημάτων τῶν προειρημένων ὑπὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
1:17.targetText: but you, beloved, remember the sayings spoken before by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ,

groups.note: Actual genitive article and Lord noun jointly supply of ... Lord as the apostles qualifier. Our and the following Jesus/Christ names retain their own separate actual anchors.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:18.sourceText: ὅτι ἔλεγον ὑμῖν Ἐπ’ ἐσχάτου τοῦ χρόνου ἔσονται ἐμπαῖκται κατὰ τὰς ἑαυτῶν ἐπιθυμίας πορευόμενοι τῶν ἀσεβειῶν.
1:18.targetText: that they said to you, that in the last time there will be scoffers, following after their own lusts of impieties,

groups.note: Actual genitive article and impieties noun jointly supply of impieties as the lusts qualifier. The separately printed following participle and reflexive possessor retain their distinct source identities.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV supplies a second reporting that to introduce the quoted warning; the initial actual ὅτι introduces they said to you and is anchored there.

1:19.sourceText: Οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἀποδιορίζοντες, ψυχικοί, Πνεῦμα μὴ ἔχοντες.
1:19.targetText: these are those causing divisions, natural men, not having the Spirit.

1:20.sourceText: ὑμεῖς δέ, ἀγαπητοί, ἐποικοδομοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς τῇ ἁγιωτάτῃ ὑμῶν πίστει, ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ προσευχόμενοι,
1:20.targetText: But you, beloved, building yourselves up on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:21.sourceText: ἑαυτοὺς ἐν ἀγάπῃ Θεοῦ τηρήσατε, προσδεχόμενοι τὸ ἔλεος τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
1:21.targetText: keep yourselves in the love of God, waiting for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ [resulting] in continuous life;

groups.note: Actual genitive article and Lord noun jointly supply of ... Lord as the mercy qualifier. Our and Jesus/Christ retain separate actual anchors; the earlier God occurrence remains distinct.

The actual goal/result preposition εἰς marks the movement toward life. English makes this result relation explicit with bracketed resulting in; resulting is not an independently written Greek participle.

1:22.targetText: and, indeed, show mercy to those who are doubting,

1:23.sourceText: σῴζετε ἐκ πυρὸς ἁρπάζοντες, οὓς δὲ ἐλεᾶτε ἐν φόβῳ, μισοῦντες καὶ τὸν ἀπὸ τῆς σαρκὸς ἐσπιλωμένον χιτῶνα.
1:23.targetText: and rescue others by snatching [them] out of fire; but show mercy to others in fear, hating even the coat having been stained from the flesh.

groups.note: The actual snatching participle gives the rescue means, rendered by snatching; by expresses the participial relation without a separately written Greek preposition.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds an opening coordination before rescue; pinned N1904 begins directly with the rescue imperative.

LSV explicitly names an additional others group as the first rescue object; N1904 has the rescue/snatching predicates without an independently written object for that first group. The actual later οὓς identifies the distinct mercy-in-fear group.
This bracketed pronoun repeats the English-added first rescue group. N1904 does not explicitly name that rescue object; the later actual relative οὓς belongs to the separate mercy-in-fear group.

review.note: The different mercy/rescue group syntax is preserved. Greek 22 explicitly has those doubting; Greek 23 begins rescue ... snatching without an independently written object, then explicitly names οὓς with the mercy-in-fear clause. The first English others and its repeated them are not falsely taken from that later distinct relative group.

1:24.sourceText: Τῷ δὲ δυναμένῳ φυλάξαι ὑμᾶς ἀπταίστους καὶ στῆσαι κατενώπιον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ ἀμώμους ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει,
1:24.targetText: And to Him who is able to guard you without stumbling, and to set [you] in the presence of His glory unblemished, in gladness,

groups.note: The actual guard object you is also the immediately coordinated set-in-glory object. English repeats the same guarded/set people as bracketed [you]; both retain that one written personal object.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:25.sourceText: μόνῳ Θεῷ Σωτῆρι ἡμῶν διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν δόξα μεγαλωσύνη κράτος καὶ ἐξουσία πρὸ παντὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος καὶ νῦν καὶ εἰς πάντας τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἀμήν.
1:25.targetText: to the only wise God our Savior, [is] glory and greatness, power and authority, both now and forever! Amen.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 explicitly includes through Jesus Christ our Lord; the pinned LSV doxology omits that intermediary-title clause.
N1904 explicitly includes before all the age/time before the now and future doxology. LSV does not render that earlier time clause; it is not exchanged for the distinct actual future-age phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds wise to only God; no corresponding Greek wise adjective is written in the pinned N1904 verse.
English supplies a copula in this nominal doxology; N1904 has the dative addressee and honor nouns without a corresponding finite be verb.
LSV explicitly coordinates glory and greatness; N1904 lists those first nouns without a conjunction.
